The Congress, recognizing the profound impact of man's activity on the interrelations of all components of the natural environment, particularly the profound influences of population growth, high density urbanization, industrial expansion, resource exploitation, and new and expanding technological advances ... declares that it is the continuing policy of the Federal Government ... to use all practical means and measures ... to create and maintain conditions under which man and nature can exist in productive harmony, and fulfill the social, economic, and other requirements of present and future generations of Americans.
One of the means by which this policy is implemented is the environmental impact statement required by sec. 102(2)(c) of the Act. In order to function meaningfully, an impact statement must take account of basic environmental values, and document precisely the way in which they are threatened or enhanced by the proposed action under consideration.
Executive Order 11644 notes that ORVs are used "... in frequent conflict with wise land and resource management practices, environmental values, and other types of recreational activity ..."

The purpose of the order, explicitly stated in sec. 1, is to
... ensure that the use of off-road vehicles on public lands will be controlled and directed so as to protect the resources of those lands, to promote the safety of all users of those lands, and to minimize the conflicts among the uses of those lands.
The Executive Order refers again to these purposes in section 3, directing that they form the basis for administrative designation of zones which will be open or closed to ORV use. These purposes make explicit the duty of the Interior Department to identify the values of the public lands that deserve protection from the impacts of ORV.
